product_family: Apple Translate: a free, system-integrated translation app for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and watchOS, supporting 20+ languages with on-device and cloud-based processing, including live translation with AirPods.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 27001
certifications.proof_quote: Apple holds ISO/IEC 27001 certification, but Translate is not in scope. Apple's certifications page lists the in-scope internet services as 'Apple accessory services, Apple Business Essentials, Apple Business Manager, Apple Messages for Business, Apple Push Notification service (APNs), Apple School Manager, Claris Connect, Claris Studio, Digital Car Key Services, FaceTime, FileMaker Cloud, iCloud, iMessage, iWork services, Managed Apple Accounts, Schoolwork, Siri' - Translate is not among them. No public evidence Translate is covered.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 27018
certifications.proof_quote: Apple holds ISO/IEC 27018 (PII protection in cloud) certification covering the same internet services scope as its ISO/IEC 27001 certificate; Translate is not among the listed in-scope services. No public evidence Translate is covered.

certifications.name: SOC 2 (Type 1/2)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of Apple or Translate holding SOC 2 certification. Apple's published certifications page focuses on ISO standards, FIPS 140-2/-3, and Common Criteria.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: Apple Translate explicitly states it 'should not be relied on in circumstances where you could be harmed or injured, in high-risk situations, for navigation, or for the diagnosis or treatment of any medical condition.' This disqualifies it from HIPAA-regulated use.

certifications.name: GDPR Compliance Posture
certifications.proof_quote: Apple's privacy governance program references compliance with 'the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA),' and Apple provides GDPR data-subject controls (access, correct, download, delete) through its privacy portal.

certifications.name: FIPS 140-3
certifications.proof_quote: Apple's security certifications page states: 'Apple maintains independent certifications and attestations over its operating system in conformance with the U.S. Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) 140-3 for cryptographic modules.' Only FIPS 140-3 is currently documented on Apple's page; the retired FIPS 140-2 predecessor is not named there. This is an operating-system-level cryptographic module certification, not Translate-specific.

certifications.name: Common Criteria
certifications.proof_quote: Apple's security certifications page states Apple holds 'Common Criteria for operating systems and device services.' This is an OS/device-level certification, not Translate-specific.

certifications.name: Global CBPR (Cross-Border Privacy Rules)
certifications.proof_quote: Apple's privacy governance page states Apple 'abides by the Global Cross-Border Privacy Rules (CBPR) System' and has held 'privacy accountability certifications for its global privacy program since 2014.' Company-wide, not Translate-specific.

certifications.name: Global Privacy Recognition for Processors (PRP)
certifications.proof_quote: Apple's privacy governance page states Apple holds the 'Global Privacy Recognition for Processors (PRP) System' certification (Global PRP System Certification Mark). Company-wide, not Translate-specific.

privacy.ai_training_note: Apple may review a subset of transcripts and text inputs for improving Translate, Siri, and other natural language processing features. Users can opt into enhanced data collection via 'Improve Siri & Dictation' in Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements, or avoid data transmission entirely by enabling On-Device Mode for downloaded languages.
privacy.data_region: Not publicly specified; Apple's privacy page states requests are processed by Apple infrastructure, region not disclosed

security.name: Encryption in transit
security.value: Assumed TLS/HTTPS for client-server communication; no explicit cipher suite published for Translate

security.name: On-device processing
security.value: Full on-device ML inference for translation when both language models are downloaded; no data sent to Apple servers

security.name: Data anonymization
security.value: Cloud-based translation associated with random rotating identifier, not Apple Account or email; not linkable to user identity by default

security.name: Data retention
security.value: Apple stores transcripts and text inputs for two years; a small subset of reviewed requests may be kept beyond two years for ongoing improvement of Translate

security.name: Live Translation with AirPods
security.value: Fully on-device for iOS 16+; supports English (US/UK), French, German, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish (Spain)

products.name: Apple Translate (iOS/iPadOS)
products.data_scope: User text and voice input; camera-based text recognition; conversation transcripts
products.notes: Free, built-in app; supports 20 languages; on-device and cloud modes available

products.name: Apple Translate (macOS)
products.data_scope: User text input; system-wide translation via right-click menu
products.notes: Free, integrated into macOS; same language support as iOS

products.name: Live Translation with AirPods
products.data_scope: Voice conversation audio; processed entirely on-device
products.notes: Requires AirPods Pro 2 or AirPods 4; on-device only; limited language support (5 languages)

compare.pricing_model: Free (included with iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS)
compare.data_residency: Not disclosed; processed by Apple infrastructure

flags: Apple Translate is not explicitly listed as in-scope for Apple's ISO 27001 or ISO 27018 certifications; only named services (iCloud, FaceTime, iMessage, Business Manager) are documented as covered.
No HIPAA compliance. Apple explicitly warns against Translate for healthcare, diagnosis, or high-risk scenarios, despite medical/business marketing in some contexts.

Data used for AI training: Apple stores transcripts for two years and reviews a small subset that may be kept beyond two years for Translate improvement; opt-out is via On-Device Mode. Users may not expect this.
Data region not disclosed: Apple does not publicly specify geographic processing locations for Translate requests.
